_README: Reader-facing prose that DESCRIBES A MECHANISM is a claim about the present
tense. This file pins each such claim to the thing that makes it true, so the
two cannot drift apart in either direction.
WHY THIS EXISTS. On 2026-08-16 the privacy page was rewritten to be true of a
feedback system that had been built but not yet wired: the page said 'Some
pages carry a feedback widget' when no page loaded feedback.js, and promised
90/180/30-day deletion clocks that only purge-feedback.py enforces, which no
workflow scheduled. The contract had recorded that the privacy page must not
LAG the widget. Nobody had written down that it must not LEAD it either.
A promise about a mechanism that does not run is the same class of lie as a
mechanism that runs unpromised -- and it is worse, because a visitor may hand
over an address on the strength of it. 'We delete your contact details after
90 days' is FALSE until something deletes them.
auto-deploy-on-push.yml fires ~4x/day gated on nothing, so 'it will be true by
the time anyone reads it' is not available as a defence.
HOW TO ADD AN ENTRY. Write the CONSTRAINT, never the value -- the same rule
content/campaigns/README.md 2.1 learned the hard way. 'requires' names a
condition this repo can evaluate today; if nothing here can check it, the claim
does not belong in reader-facing prose yet.
PREDICATE KINDS:
page_loads_script   some HTML under public/ references this path
workflow_schedules  some workflow has a cron AND invokes this script
path_exists         this path exists in the repo
The checker FAILS CLOSED: an unknown predicate kind, a missing claim_file, or a
malformed entry rejects the WHOLE registry rather than skipping the entry. A
skipped entry resurfaces later as a fresh finding and sends someone hunting a
bug nobody introduced.
KNOWN WEAKNESS OF workflow_schedules -- read before trusting its green.
It proves a script is INVOKED BY a workflow that carries a cron. It does NOT
prove the run can reach the data it is supposed to act on.
That gap is live right now, not theoretical. The feedback store is on DreamHost
shared hosting; a GitHub runner has no store, so `purge-feedback.py --check`
exits 2 (UNKNOWN) there by design. A cron on ubuntu-latest would therefore
delete nothing, check nothing, and still satisfy this predicate -- turning the
guard into the very thing it was written to catch, one level up. The predicate
is a necessary condition, never a sufficient one.
Until a predicate can assert reachability, the retention claim below is only as
good as the human who wired the workflow. Do not read its green as 'contact
fields are being deleted'. Read it as 'something is scheduled, go look at what'.

claims.why: The page tells visitors a widget exists and describes what it stores. If no page mounts it, the description is of a thing that is not there, and every retention promise attached to it is unanchored.

A retention policy without a cron job is prose -- the contract says so in section 10 and then the privacy page shipped the prose first anyway. Nothing deletes a contact field unless purge-feedback.py runs on a schedule.

The page tells visitors their feedback may be counted in a public tally, and that only counts are published. If nothing generates that file the promise describes nothing, and the k=5 suppression rule it also promises protects nobody.

We store no identity, so the receipt is the ONLY key by which a person can ask to be erased. Offering that route with no tool behind it makes an unkeepable promise to the one visitor who most wants it kept.
